:

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondents not to forcibly remove or demolish the shop of the petitioner pursuant to an announcement made in the locality that the shops standing in Sakchi Market Area, Jamshedpur will be demolished.
2. In I.A. No.9561 of 2017, the petitioner has prayed for restraining the respondents from taking any coercive measure to demolish the shop of the petitioner.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner runs a betel shop, situated at Daru Bhatti Road, Line No.22, Kasidih Chowk, P.O. & P.S. Sakchi, Jamshedpur, District East Singhbhum.
The father of the petitioner had been carrying out the business activity of betel shop since decades and after the demise of his father, the petitioner has been carrying out the said business.

Learned counsel further submits that a trade licence was granted by the respondent-Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee in the year 1987 itself and the licence fee for the said betel shop has been paid by the petitioner till the year 2017-18.

The petitioner has also been granted a registration certificate under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on 15th June, 2017, which is valid for a Sita Ram Sharma vs State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 14 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183878625/
1 period of five years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that in the last week of November, 2017, the respondents visited the shop of the petitioner and asked him to vacate the same failing which the said shop would be demolished.

It is, thus, submitted that the respondents may demolish the shop of the petitioner without any formal notice or proceeding and with the aforesaid apprehension the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent-State and Jamshedpur Notified Area Committee jointly submit that it is not clear from the writ petition that any notice for evicting the petitioner from his place of business has been issued or not.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on going through the content of the writ petition, it appears that no notice for removal of encroachment/eviction of the petitioner from his place of business has been brought on record.

However, it has been stated in the writ petition that in the last week of November, 2017, the respondent authorities had visited the said area and the petitioner was asked by them to vacate the premises failing which he shall be evicted from there forcibly.
Since no notice of eviction or for demolition of the shop of the petitioner has been annexed in the present writ petition, no positive order can be passed by this Court at present.

6. However, the petitioner is at liberty to move before the respondent no.2-Deputy Commissioner,
East Singhbhum by filing representation, including the request for rehabilitation as per the provisions of Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 and Rules/policies framed thereunder.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The respondent no.2, in turn, shall decide the representation of the petitioner, keeping in mind the provisions of the Act, 2014, Rules and policies.
7. It is made clear that the respondent authorities shall take any step to evict the petitioner from his place of business in question after following the due procedure, as provided under the law.
8. This writ petition is disposed of with the aforesaid liberty, observations and directions.
9. In view of the order passed in the writ petition, I.A. No.9561 of 2017 also stands disposed of.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Sanjay/
